speaker: Doctor
text: That's an unusual complaint. How would you describe the sensation of the "shooting" pain, and does it radiate to any other area of your head or neck?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Is the shooting pain strictly triggered by chewing or jaw movement, and does pressing on your jaw joint (TMJ) reproduce that sensation? Please also confirm if the pain occurs when you move your jaw laterally.

REQUEST TEST: Temporal_Mandibular_Joint_Imaging
REQUEST IMAGES: TMJ_XRay

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your TMJ imaging is normal, the pain likely isn't originating from the joint itself. Given the shooting nature of the pain and your history of ear issues, could you tell me if the pain worsens when you close your mouth tightly or when you try to move your earlobe? Also, have you noticed any specific discharge or fullness in the right ear recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Occipital Neuralgia (secondary to chronic tension and prior ear surgery scarring)

Given the normal TMJ workup and the specific trigger of wearing earrings (tugging on scar tissue) combined with stress-induced pain, this suggests nerve irritation rather than a joint disorder. Do you experience any tingling or numbness on the back of your scalp or behind the ear?
